texts: Bilateral coni are present in over 75 percent of patients with DORV and a subaortic VSD: B.
In DORV both great arteries usually sit on muscular coni (infundibula), so neither semilunar valve is in fibrous continuity with the mitral valve.
The subaortic VSD is the most common type; the Taussig-Bing heart has a subpulmonary VSD, and noncommitted VSDs go with complete AV canal defects.
In the picture, three of the four hotels with the hole under the orca have two funnels, one under each great vessel.
